Big Guns! Navy Training Film on Battleship Main Gun Operation and Firing

Recently I've been playing World of Warships which is a free to play game that I am really quite enjoying. Anyway I've finally worked my way up to some of the big battleships and while they are extremely powerful, have a very long range, and a lot of armor, they have equal downsides that can be taken advantage of if you don't have any support vessels around you. For instance battleships are very slow to maneuver and even slower to rotate their guns around to sight in a target, I mean painfully slow. This means you have to plan way ahead of time to get the most out of them.

I decided to watch some videos of these ships in real life operation to get a better understanding of why it takes upwards of 30 seconds to reload these guns, which is an eternity when you are getting shot at. It takes 79 men to operate one single triple gun battery! This one shows the entire process of loading and firing these mammoth 16" guns that can go over 20 miles, beyond the horizon at sea accurately. Some of these ships have 6 batteries which means a team of 474 men simply operating main guns alone. And the size of the triple gun battery including its lower gearing and ammunition delivery system is roughly the size of a fairly large 3 story house.

I can't even imagine being fired at by one of these things and trying to return fire. The sound must knock you flat. It must be hard to keep your composure in those situations, while knowing that your reload speed and the skill of the teammates helping you reload the weapons could make the difference between life and death.
